nodes.name: AbstractBackupProvider.java
nodes.summary: Abstract base implementation for backup providers, handling common backup lifecycle plumbing so concrete providers only override operation-specific methods.

nodes.name: BackupExecutionProvider.java
nodes.summary: Interface for executing individual backup jobs. Implementors run the actual backup operation and return a BackupResult.

nodes.name: Plugin.java
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for all Morpheus plugins. Plugin authors extend this class, override initialize() to register PluginProviders, and set plugin metadata (name, author, version). It holds the provider registry, a reference to PluginManager, and the MorpheusContext.

nodes.name: PluginInterface.java
nodes.summary: Interface contract for all Plugin implementations. Declares the initialize() lifecycle hook and metadata accessors that every plugin must fulfil.

nodes.name: PluginManager.java
nodes.summary: Manages the lifecycle of all loaded plugins within Morpheus. Responsible for loading, initializing, and unloading Plugin instances. Provides a registry for looking up registered providers by type.

nodes.name: StorageVolume.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a block storage volume.

nodes.name: MorpheusSecurityGroupService.java
nodes.summary: Service for managing SecurityGroup records and syncing security group state from cloud platforms.

nodes.name: MorpheusServices.java
nodes.summary: Service registry interface exposing getters for every Morpheus domain service (network, cloud, compute, storage, identity, etc.). Retrieved from MorpheusContext; follows the facade pattern so providers interact with one consistent entry point.

nodes.name: Workload.java
nodes.summary: Model for a single workload (container/VM) within an Instance. Provisioning providers interact with this when starting, stopping, or removing individual workload units.

nodes.name: ServiceResponse.java
nodes.summary: Generic response envelope returned by all PluginProvider methods. Contains a success flag, message, field-level error map for UI display, typed data payload, and an inProgress flag for async operations. This is the universal return contract enforced across the entire SDK.

nodes.name: ProvisionProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for provisioning workloads. Covers the full instance lifecycle: runWorkload, stopWorkload, restartWorkload, removeWorkload. Used by Morpheus when an instance is created through the UI or API.

nodes.name: ReportProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for custom reporting. Implementors return report HTML or structured data displayed in the Morpheus Reporting section.

nodes.name: SecurityGroupProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for security group management. Handles creating, updating, and removing security groups and their rules on a cloud or network platform.

nodes.name: ServerTabProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for adding custom tabs to the server (host) detail page.

nodes.name: StorageProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for storage integrations. Implementors expose volume, bucket, and file-share lifecycle operations backed by an external storage system.

nodes.name: InputTypeLibraryProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for registering custom OptionType input renderers. Implementors add new input types that can be referenced by code in OptionType field definitions.

nodes.name: InstanceTabProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for adding custom tabs to the instance detail page. Implementors return rendered HTML for the tab content via getRenderer().

nodes.name: IPAMProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for IP Address Management integrations. Declares allocateIp, releaseIp, and network pool synchronisation to let Morpheus manage IPs through external IPAM systems.

nodes.name: LlmProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for Large Language Model integrations. Exposes a completion/chat API so Morpheus AI features can use external LLM providers.

nodes.name: Instance.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a Morpheus Instance — an application deployment that may span one or more ComputeServers. Contains name, layout, owner, and lifecycle state.

nodes.name: CloudProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for cloud integrations. Implementors sync virtual machines, networks, and storage from a cloud platform into Morpheus and expose cloud-specific lifecycle hooks (refresh, validateCloudConfig).

nodes.name: MorpheusStorageVolumeService.java
nodes.summary: Service for managing StorageVolume records. Used by provisioning and storage providers to track block volumes.

nodes.name: MorpheusSynchronousDataService.java
nodes.summary: Blocking (synchronous) variant of MorpheusDataService. Returns plain values instead of Observables; intended for contexts where the reactive overhead is unnecessary.

nodes.name: ChildFirstClassLoader.java
nodes.summary: Custom ClassLoader that prioritizes plugin jar classes over parent (morpheus-ui) classes. Enables plugin isolation — two plugins can ship different versions of the same dependency without conflict.

nodes.name: NetworkProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for network integrations. Covers network CRUD, subnet management, security groups, and load balancers backed by an external network platform.

nodes.name: PluginProvider.java
nodes.summary: Root interface for all Morpheus provider types. Defines the shared contract (getCode, getName, isEnabled) that every integration provider must implement.

nodes.name: VirtualImage.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a cloud image or VM template that can be used for provisioning.

nodes.name: OptionType.java
nodes.summary: Data model representing a single form input field in Morpheus. Contains the input type code, field label, default value, validation rules, visibility conditions (visibleOnCode/requireOnCode), and dependency chain (dependsOn). Used everywhere a user-facing form is defined.

nodes.name: MorpheusTaskService.java
nodes.summary: Service for managing Task and task execution records. Used by TaskProviders to interact with Morpheus automation objects.

nodes.name: MorpheusVirtualImageService.java
nodes.summary: Service for managing VirtualImage records — images/templates that can be provisioned. Providers use this to sync available images from their cloud platform.

nodes.name: ComputeServer.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a managed VM or bare-metal server (host). Central entity in cloud and provisioning flows — contains OS, hardware spec, network config, and lifecycle state.

nodes.name: TaskProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for automation tasks. Plugin authors implement executeTask() to create reusable automation steps that run within Morpheus workflows and task sets.

nodes.name: UIExtensionProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for injecting custom content into the Morpheus UI. Implementations add scripts, stylesheets, or HTML fragments that load alongside the standard Morpheus frontend.

nodes.name: WizardProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for wizard step definitions. Each step declares input OptionTypes, validation logic, and navigation rules. Used in combination with ConfigurationWorkflowProvider.

nodes.name: MorpheusIdentityService.java
nodes.summary: Service providing identity and authentication operations for plugins — user lookup, permission checks, and session validation.

nodes.name: MorpheusInstanceService.java
nodes.summary: Service for querying Instance records. Gives providers a read handle to the Morpheus instance (application deployment) model.

nodes.name: BackupRestoreProvider.java
nodes.summary: Interface for restoring from a backup. Implementors take a BackupResult and restore the workload to the recorded snapshot.

nodes.name: BackupResult.java
nodes.summary: Model capturing the outcome of a single backup execution — status, size, location, and any errors.

nodes.name: MorpheusComputeServerService.java
nodes.summary: Service for querying and managing ComputeServer (VM/bare-metal host) records. Used by CloudProviders to sync inventory and update server state.

nodes.name: MorpheusContext.java
nodes.summary: Central dependency-injection handle passed to every PluginProvider. Grants access to all MorpheusServices, the async services facade, and other runtime capabilities. Plugins hold the context instance and access services through it rather than constructing their own.

nodes.name: MorpheusDataService.java
nodes.summary: Generic reactive CRUD service interface. Provides list, get, create, save, and remove operations returning RxJava observables. The base abstraction that most domain services extend.

nodes.name: TaskConfig.java
nodes.summary: Model carrying the execution context for a task run — includes the target server, instance, and configuration variables.

nodes.name: Renderer.java
nodes.summary: Interface for template rendering. Implementations (e.g. Handlebars renderer) take a template name and model map and return rendered HTML strings for custom tabs and UI extensions.

nodes.name: Cloud.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a Morpheus cloud integration record. Holds cloud type, credentials reference, sync settings, and associated compute zones.

nodes.name: Network.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a network resource (VPC, VLAN, subnet, etc.).

nodes.name: ConfigurationWorkflowProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for multi-step configuration wizards. Returns a WizardProvider that drives the step-by-step UI flow, enabling plugins to embed guided setup experiences in the Morpheus interface.

nodes.name: CredentialProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for credential integrations. Allows Morpheus to retrieve credentials from external secrets managers (e.g. HashiCorp Vault, CyberArk).

nodes.name: DatasetProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for dynamic datasets. Implementations supply data for typeahead and dropdown inputs in forms, backed by live queries to external systems.

nodes.name: DNSProvider.java
nodes.summary: Provider interface for DNS integrations (e.g. AWS Route53, Infoblox). Declares create/update/delete DNS record operations and zone-level synchronisation methods.

nodes.name: MorpheusAsyncServices.java
nodes.summary: Async (RxJava Observable/Maybe/Single) variant of the Morpheus service layer. All read/write operations here are non-blocking and return reactive streams rather than plain values.

nodes.name: Permission.java
nodes.summary: Model representing a Morpheus RBAC permission. Plugins declare required permissions so Morpheus can enforce access control on plugin-provided features.

layers.name: Plugin Framework
layers.description: Core plugin lifecycle: Plugin base class, PluginInterface contract, PluginManager lifecycle, and ChildFirstClassLoader isolation. This is the entry point every plugin author touches first.

layers.name: Provider Interfaces
layers.description: All PluginProvider sub-interfaces that define integration contracts for Cloud, DNS, IPAM, Provisioning, Backup, Storage, Network, Tasks, UI extensions, Reporting, Credential, Configuration Workflow, Dataset, LLM, and more.

layers.name: Context & Services (Morpheus API)
layers.description: MorpheusContext is the DI handle; MorpheusServices aggregates all domain services (network, compute, storage, identity, backup, etc.) using RxJava reactive streams. This layer bridges plugins and the Morpheus data platform.

layers.name: Data Models
layers.description: POJO model classes in com.morpheusdata.model representing all Morpheus domain objects: Cloud, ComputeServer, Instance, Workload, Network, VirtualImage, StorageVolume, OptionType, Permission, and hundreds more.

layers.name: Request / Response API
layers.description: ServiceResponse<T> is the universal return type for all provider operations. Request models in com.morpheusdata.request carry structured input to provider methods.

layers.name: Views & Web
layers.description: Renderer interface and Handlebars view support (com.morpheusdata.views); PluginController base for plugin-exposed HTTP endpoints (com.morpheusdata.web).

layers.name: Backup Domain
layers.description: Specialised sub-domain under core/backup: BackupProvider, BackupExecutionProvider, BackupRestoreProvider, and their abstract base implementations, plus dedicated Morpheus backup services.

layers.name: Build Tooling
layers.description: morpheus-plugin-gradle Gradle plugin that handles plugin JAR assembly, manifest generation, and publishing for plugin projects consuming this SDK.

layers.name: Sample Plugins
layers.description: Reference implementations under samples/ that demonstrate SDK usage patterns for plugin authors.

tour.title: Where every plugin begins — Plugin.java
tour.description: The Plugin abstract class is ground zero for any Morpheus plugin. A plugin author extends Plugin, overrides initialize(), registers one or more PluginProviders, and sets metadata (name, version, author). When Morpheus loads a plugin JAR it instantiates this class first, making it the natural entry point for understanding the whole system.

tour.title: The provider contract — PluginProvider
tour.description: PluginProvider (in core/providers/) is the root interface every integration type extends. It declares getCode(), getName(), and isEnabled() — the minimum a provider must expose. From here, over 40 specialised sub-interfaces branch out for every integration category (Cloud, DNS, IPAM, Backup, UI, and more). Understanding this interface makes the entire provider hierarchy navigable.

tour.title: Connecting to a cloud — CloudProvider and ProvisionProvider
tour.description: CloudProvider handles inventory sync (VMs, networks, storage) from a cloud platform; ProvisionProvider handles the provisioning lifecycle (create, start, stop, remove workloads). Together they cover the full cloud integration surface. Both are in core/providers/ and return ServiceResponse on every operation.

tour.title: The universal return type — ServiceResponse
tour.description: Every provider method returns a ServiceResponse<T>. It carries a success flag, human-readable message, field-level error map for UI display, typed data payload, and an inProgress flag for async workflows. Understanding this class is essential before reading any provider implementation because it is the protocol between plugins and morpheus-ui.

tour.title: Accessing Morpheus data — MorpheusContext and MorpheusServices
tour.description: MorpheusContext is the single dependency-injection handle injected into every provider. Calling context.getServices() returns MorpheusServices, a facade that exposes typed service objects for every Morpheus domain (compute, network, storage, identity, backup, and more). All data reads and writes flow through this chain, keeping the plugin boundary clean.

tour.title: Reactive data access — MorpheusDataService
tour.description: MorpheusDataService defines the generic reactive CRUD interface. Every domain service (MorpheusComputeServerService, MorpheusNetworkService, MorpheusVirtualImageService, and more) extends it and returns RxJava Observable/Maybe/Single. Providers subscribe to these streams to list, create, save, and remove domain objects without blocking.

tour.title: Domain objects — models
tour.description: com.morpheusdata.model holds all POJO domain objects. ComputeServer represents a VM/host, Instance represents a deployed application, Network represents a network resource, and OptionType represents a UI form field. These are the objects providers receive and return; studying a few key models clarifies the data contract between Morpheus and plugins.

tour.title: Building forms — OptionType and wizard providers
tour.description: OptionType is the field-level model for Morpheus forms: it captures input type, label, default value, visibility conditions (visibleOnCode/requireOnCode), and dependency chains. WizardProvider and DatasetProvider build on OptionType to power multi-step configuration wizards with dynamic dropdowns backed by live dataset queries.

tour.title: Extending the UI — tabs and UI extension providers
tour.description: InstanceTabProvider, ServerTabProvider, and UIExtensionProvider let plugins inject HTML into the Morpheus frontend. The Renderer interface (Handlebars-based) converts template files in the plugin JAR into rendered HTML. This is how plugins add context-aware UI panels without forking morpheus-ui.

tour.title: A working example — VolumeTabSamplePlugin
tour.description: The sample plugin under samples/morpheus-volume-tab-plugin is the canonical reference. It extends Plugin, registers a VolumeTabProvider, and renders a Handlebars template. Tracing this sample end-to-end (from Plugin.initialize() through the provider to the renderer) demonstrates every concept from the previous nine stops applied together.
